Director of Operations

Job Description

Compensation: $150,000-$160,000 per year

This role will be based out of Atlanta, GA; New York, NY; or Detroit, MI.

Job Overview

The Operations Director will be responsible for directing and implementing company policy to ensure compliance with contract responsibilities.

Roles & Responsibilities

Manage costs and revenue to meet company top and bottom-line financial goals including:
Expanding business within Strategic Accounts / Clients, negotiating increases with Customers, reduction of operating costs, and or changes in schedules or processes
Directing operations necessary, both directly and through subordinate managers, to carry out contractual responsibilities and profitability that meet both the Customer’s contractual expectations but to exceed their service expectations resulting in the creation of complete Customer satisfaction.
Maintain a safe work environment for self and employees by implementing comprehensive safety, recognition, and training programs
Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal regulations, such as FLSA, OSHA, ADA, etc.
Budget compliance for identified Accounts
Manage and retain a qualified (individually or through subordinate) staff that is reasonably satisfied with position and compensation, understands, and is trained for their position and has a clear line of sight to the goals and expectations of the company and recognized the impact their contributions to the Company

The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Bachelor’s degree in business, communications, or a related field from a four-year college or university with 5-10 years of experience; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations

May be required to have a valid driver’s license.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Carries out management responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, planning, assigning, and directing work; performance evaluations; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems. jobs.title: Head of Operations / Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description:

InterCapital is an alternative investment manager focused primarily on long/short public equities. Since its inception in 2021, the firm has built a strong investment track record while significantly expanding its institutional infrastructure and investor base. The firm is seeking a Head of Operations / Chief Operating Officer to help support its continued growth. The firm runs a long/short public equity hedge fund (InterCapital Fund, LP) a generalist fund focused on high-conviction ideas. InterCapital combines bottom-up fundamental security selection with top-down market awareness, including selective use of options to enhance convexity, hedge exposures, and capitalize on dislocations.

Role Description:

Operations Support

Oversee cash reconciliations, and corporate actions across prime brokerage and custody relationships
Maintain and improve operational infrastructure, internal controls, and documented procedures
Manage counterparty and vendor relationships: administrator, prime broker(s), auditor, legal, IT/cybersecurity, and data providers — including diligence, negotiation, and ongoing service review
Oversee the monthly NAV process with the fund administrator, including review of valuations, reconciliations, and fee calculations (management and incentive)
Manage the annual audit and tax cycle, coordinating with the auditor and tax advisors on financial statements, K-1s, and estimates
Direct treasury and cash management, including capital activity, expense management, and the management company's finances

Compliance & Regulatory

Administer the firm's compliance program as an SEC-registered investment adviser, working with outside compliance counsel/consultants
Help in consultation with our compliance team on regulatory filings and deadlines (e.g., Form ADV, Form PF, 13F, N-PX) and marketing-rule compliance for the fund's Rule 506(c) offering
Maintain books and records, personal trading oversight, and annual compliance reviews

Investor Relations & Operations

Manage investor onboarding, subscriptions, redemptions, and KYC/AML in coordination with the administrator
Support LP communications: monthly performance reporting, investor letters, DDQs, and ad hoc requests
Help institutionalize the firm's IR infrastructure as the LP base grows

Business Development & Firm Growth

Partner with the Founder on capital raising: build and manage the prospect pipeline, and leverage the fund's Rule 506(c) designation to support compliant marketing and outreach to new limited partners
Lead the operational and structural workstreams for potential new vehicles under the InterCapital umbrella — including an offshore fund structure to support international expansion and non-U.S. investors — coordinating legal, tax, and administration through launch
Help scale the firm's infrastructure, service-provider relationships, and processes ahead of AUM and product growth

Qualifications:

Advanced Excel skills; comfort building and improving processes and systems from the ground up
Self-directed operator who thrives with broad responsibility in a small-team environment; highest standards of integrity and discretion
Strong operations management skills, including process design, workflow optimization, and oversight of middle- and back-office functions.
Advanced analytical skills for evaluating operational data, risk metrics, and performance reports, and for supporting decision-making and problem-solving.
Team management capabilities, including experience leading distributed teams, setting priorities, and fostering accountability.
Excellent communication skills for collaborating with investment professionals, service providers, and investors, and for producing clear written documentation.
Budgeting and financial management skills, including experience with cost control, resource planning, and vendor negotiation.
Experience in investment management, hedge funds, or asset management operations, with familiarity in long/short equity strategies and related infrastructure.
Knowledge of regulatory and compliance frameworks relevant to investment firms, and experience implementing operational controls and best practices.

Compensation:

InterCapital offers a highly competitive compensation package designed to align with the seniority and responsibility of the role. Compensation will include a competitive base salary, annual performance-based bonus opportunity, and the potential for meaningful long-term economic participation in the growth and success of the firm through equity. The ultimate package will be tailored based on the candidate’s experience, capabilities, and ability to take broad ownership of the firm’s operational infrastructure.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Executive Director
(ED) provides overall strategic, operational, and financial leadership for HFH7RM, working in close partnership with the Board of Directors, staff, volunteers, and community partners. The ED advances the mission through effective program oversight, innovative fundraising, careful financial stewardship, and enthusiastic community engagement.

The successful candidate will embody Habitat’s core values of integrity, respect, compassion, and accountability, and will lead with creativity, collaboration, and a commitment to organizational, financial, and environmental sustainability.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership & Administration
Provide day-to-day leadership and management of HFH7RM operations in alignment with Board-approved policies and strategic priorities.
Hire, supervise, mentor, and evaluate staff; foster a positive, inclusive, and mission-driven workplace culture.
Oversee staff responsible for volunteer recruitment, engagement, and training.
Ensure compliance with Habitat for Humanity International standards, affiliate requirements, and all applicable laws and regulations.
Represent the affiliate at conferences and professional development opportunities.

Finance & Resource Development

Provide overall financial leadership, including budget oversight, financial planning, and long-term fiscal sustainability.
Lead the development and implementation of new major donor campaigns and planned giving initiatives as well as support current fundraising strategies and grant writing.
Work with staff and the Board of Directors to develop, monitor, and report on annual budgets.
Authorize expenditures within Board-approved guidelines.
Serve as lead contact for outside auditing agency every year.
Monitor and maintain appropriate insurance coverage.

Board Partnership & Governance Support

Work collaboratively with the Board of Directors, attending all Board meetings and supporting committee work as needed.
Support Board development, including orientation and ongoing training of Board members.
Provide timely, accurate, and relevant reports on organizational performance, finances, and strategic initiatives.
Assist the Board with strategic planning, goal setting, and long-term organizational sustainability.

Programs & ReStore Oversight

Provide executive oversight of all affiliate programs, including new home construction, weatherization, and critical home repair.
Collaborate with staff, committees, and volunteers to ensure program quality, consistency, safety, and funding alignment.
Work with partners and committees to identify and secure suitable building sites.
Support the ReStore Manager in pursuing operational excellence and revenue growth.
Encourage retail best practices to maximize mission-aligned income generation.
Maintain appropriate engagement with Habitat for Humanity International and ASO–Habitat of Maine program teams to strengthen and expand affiliate programming.

Community Engagement & Public Relations

Serve as the primary spokesperson for HFH7RM within the community.
Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, faith partners, businesses, civic organizations, and local government.
Support visibility and awareness of HFH7RM through public speaking, outreach, and media engagement.
Collaborate with staff on communications, marketing, and social media to strengthen the organization’s public presence.

Facilities & Property Management

Oversee maintenance of the office and ReStore facilities.
Manage relationships with property owners and facility management partners.
Oversee maintenance of trucks, vans, and trailers used by the Restore and the Critical Home Repair teams.
Support annual facilities budgeting and long-term maintenance planning.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree required; an equivalent combination of education and significant relevant experience may be considered.
Minimum of five years of leadership experience in nonprofit management, marketing/public relations, construction, housing, or community development.
Experience with fundraising, donor relations, and/or resource development.
Ability to supervise, mentor, and lead staff and volunteers effectively.
Experience with budgeting, financial oversight, and organizational management.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to build productive partnerships with community and governmental organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with Habitat for Humanity’s mission, values, and affiliate structure.
Knowledge of residential construction or building science.
Experience with nonprofit retail operations (such as a ReStore or similar enterprise).

Additional Requirements

Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.
Ability to travel throughout the service area.
Ability to lift boxes up to 45 pounds.
Successful completion of criminal background, motor vehicle, and sex offender registry checks.

What We Offer

HFH7RM offers a competitive salary between $65,000 and $85,000, depending on experience, as well as a comprehensive benefits package, flexibility in work schedule, and a strong commitment to professional development. You’ll join a collaborative staff team, a supportive Board of Directors, and a welcoming community in Maine’s beautiful Midcoast region.

jobs.title: ERP Business Development Director – DOT
jobs.description:
Position Description

At CGI, we offer limitless opportunities to make a meaningful impact for the clients and communities we serve. CGI Advantage is a unified ERP platform featuring a powerful combination of modern technology and built-for-government solutions. With over 46 years of public sector expertise, our secure, intuitive platform is backed by an active client community that values innovation and access to CGI’s global network of experts.

We are seeking a dynamic, results driven ERP Business Development Director with strong experience working with Departments of Transportation (DOTs) to lead strategic growth initiatives and expand our footprint within State and Local Government markets. This role focuses on identifying, advancing, and closing new business opportunities by promoting our market leading ERP solutions. The ideal candidate brings proven success selling into DOT agencies, an understanding of their operational needs, and the ability to build trusted relationships with transportation leadership teams. Experience engaging with State DOTs is highly preferred and will be a key differentiator.

Location & Work Model : Open to candidates near any CGI U.S. office. Hybrid work model with travel based on project needs.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Develop and execute a comprehensive business development strategy focused on ERP solutions (e.g., Oracle, SAP, PeopleSoft, CGI Advantage, CGI Momentum, etc.), with a targeted focus on State DOT needs such as infrastructure funding, capital project accounting, asset lifecycle management, grants, and transportation financial systems.
Identify, qualify, and pursue new business opportunities with State and Local Government, especially Departments of Transportation-through market research, targeted outreach, networking, and DOT specific lead generation.
Research DOT organizational structures and decision makers; synthesize intelligence to position CGI’s ERP capabilities tailored to transportation operations, funding cycles, and federal compliance requirements.
Build and maintain strong relationships with DOT CIOs, CFOs, Chief Engineers, division directors, and other key transportation stakeholders; understand their pain points, modernization goals, and ERP transformation priorities.
Lead the end to end sales cycle including capability positioning, proposal development, RFP responses, oral presentations, contract negotiation, and deal closure within the DOT environment.
Collaborate with pre sales teams, solution architects, and delivery teams to align DOT requirements—such as project accounting, maintenance management, fleet/asset management, and federal grant compliance with the proposed ERP solution.
Establish trusted, peer level relationships across DOT agencies to effectively position CGI’s differentiators and proactively propose innovative solutions.
Represent the company at transportation industry events, DOT conferences, and government technology forums to promote CGI’s capabilities and thought leadership.
Track, manage, and report on sales pipeline, forecasts, and performance metrics, including DOT specific pursuits, to senior leadership.
Stay current on ERP and DOT industry trends, modernization initiatives, FHWA/FTA regulations, IIJA/BIL funding requirements, and competitive offerings.
Ability and willingness to travel as needed for DOT client engagement.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Public Administration, or related field (MBA preferred).
10+ years of experience in business development or sales within the ERP space, including direct experience working with any Departments of Transportation(State or Federal)
Proven track record of meeting or exceeding sales targets in enterprise software, ERP transformation programs, or government consulting services.
In-depth understanding of ERP platforms, implementation lifecycles, and transportation related workflows such as capital project management, asset management, federal grants, and state transportation finance.
Strong knowledge of government budgeting, DOT procurement processes, RFP procedures, and legislative funding cycles.
Exceptional negotiation, communication, and presentation skills, with demonstrated success influencing senior DOT executives.
Highly entrepreneurial, persistent, and persuasive, with a strong ability to navigate complex government environments and long sales cycles.
Ability to work both independently and in a collaborative, fast paced, matrixed environment.
Willingness to travel as required.

CGI anticipates accepting applications through September 30, 2026.

The determination of this range includes various factors not limited to skill set, level, experience, relevant training, and licensure and certifications. To support the ability to reward for merit-based performance, CGI typically does not hire individuals at or near the top of the range for their role. Company Description:

InterCapital is an alternative investment manager focused primarily on long/short public equities. Since its inception in 2021, the firm has built a strong investment track record while significantly expanding its institutional infrastructure and investor base. The firm is seeking a Head of Operations / Chief Operating Officer to help support its continued growth. The firm runs a long/short public equity hedge fund (InterCapital Fund, LP) a generalist fund focused on high-conviction ideas. InterCapital combines bottom-up fundamental security selection with top-down market awareness, including selective use of options to enhance convexity, hedge exposures, and capitalize on dislocations.

Role Description:

Operations Support

Oversee cash reconciliations, and corporate actions across prime brokerage and custody relationships
Maintain and improve operational infrastructure, internal controls, and documented procedures
Manage counterparty and vendor relationships: administrator, prime broker(s), auditor, legal, IT/cybersecurity, and data providers — including diligence, negotiation, and ongoing service review
Oversee the monthly NAV process with the fund administrator, including review of valuations, reconciliations, and fee calculations (management and incentive)
Manage the annual audit and tax cycle, coordinating with the auditor and tax advisors on financial statements, K-1s, and estimates
Direct treasury and cash management, including capital activity, expense management, and the management company's finances

Compliance & Regulatory

Administer the firm's compliance program as an SEC-registered investment adviser, working with outside compliance counsel/consultants
Help in consultation with our compliance team on regulatory filings and deadlines (e.g., Form ADV, Form PF, 13F, N-PX) and marketing-rule compliance for the fund's Rule 506(c) offering
Maintain books and records, personal trading oversight, and annual compliance reviews

Investor Relations & Operations

Manage investor onboarding, subscriptions, redemptions, and KYC/AML in coordination with the administrator
Support LP communications: monthly performance reporting, investor letters, DDQs, and ad hoc requests
Help institutionalize the firm's IR infrastructure as the LP base grows

Business Development & Firm Growth

Partner with the Founder on capital raising: build and manage the prospect pipeline, and leverage the fund's Rule 506(c) designation to support compliant marketing and outreach to new limited partners
Lead the operational and structural workstreams for potential new vehicles under the InterCapital umbrella — including an offshore fund structure to support international expansion and non-U.S. investors — coordinating legal, tax, and administration through launch
Help scale the firm's infrastructure, service-provider relationships, and processes ahead of AUM and product growth

Qualifications:

Advanced Excel skills; comfort building and improving processes and systems from the ground up
Self-directed operator who thrives with broad responsibility in a small-team environment; highest standards of integrity and discretion
Strong operations management skills, including process design, workflow optimization, and oversight of middle- and back-office functions.
Advanced analytical skills for evaluating operational data, risk metrics, and performance reports, and for supporting decision-making and problem-solving.
Team management capabilities, including experience leading distributed teams, setting priorities, and fostering accountability.
Excellent communication skills for collaborating with investment professionals, service providers, and investors, and for producing clear written documentation.
Budgeting and financial management skills, including experience with cost control, resource planning, and vendor negotiation.
Experience in investment management, hedge funds, or asset management operations, with familiarity in long/short equity strategies and related infrastructure.
Knowledge of regulatory and compliance frameworks relevant to investment firms, and experience implementing operational controls and best practices.

Compensation:

InterCapital offers a highly competitive compensation package designed to align with the seniority and responsibility of the role. Compensation will include a competitive base salary, annual performance-based bonus opportunity, and the potential for meaningful long-term economic participation in the growth and success of the firm through equity. Experience engaging with State DOTs is highly preferred and will be a key differentiator.

to lead 180 FTEs. In this role, you will support PM Soldier Survivability (SSV), which is located at Ft. Belvoir, VA.
